content.title: About
content.content: Chicken Burrito Bowl is a Mexican‑inspired dish served in a bowl with rice, black beans, seasoned chicken pieces, fresh vegetables, guacamole and salsa. It combines the bold flavors of spices, lean protein, and wholesome carbs for a balanced, satisfying meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bowl version emerged as a lighter alternative to the traditional wrapped burrito, offering the same ingredients without the tortilla.
Chicken is usually marinated in lime juice, chili, and cumin, giving it a distinctive aroma.
The Mexican rice used is often cooked with tomato paste and spices rather than plain boiled rice.
The dish is popular in fast‑casual chains across the US and Canada, often customizable with extra toppings.
Variations may replace chicken with beef, tofu, or seafood, but the classic chicken version remains the most common.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice and beans supply lasting energy and help maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The bowl delivers vitamin C from salsa, vitamin K and potassium from avocado, and iron from beans.

items.title: Heart‑friendly fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats in guacamole support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Beans and vegetables boost fiber content, aiding digestion.

items.title: Allergy to chicken or legumes
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or beans.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and seasonings can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: The bowl can be calorie‑rich due to avocado and sauces; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Food safety concerns
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked and beans properly boiled to avoid bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the bowl in a large dish. You can stir all ingredients together or eat them separately, adding sauces to taste. For a lighter option, reduce guacamole and swap rice for quinoa.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared bowl in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat chicken and beans to at least 75 °C. Add avocado just before serving to prevent browning.
